performed_via_github_app.description:
Publish incredibly high performance websites and applications right from GitHub. The Netlify platform connects your repositories to an all-in-one workflow for global CDN deployment, continuous integration, and automatic (and free) HTTPS. Each time you commit changes, Netlify builds your site, prerenders markup, and optimizes assets on dedicated build infrastructure. Easily create an entirely automated workflows for your web applications

## Features

### Push your site live, directly from GitHub
Deploy your site to an ultra-redundant global CDN that’s purpose built for serving pages and assets quickly and consistently.

### Automate deployment
Netlify’s built-in Continuous Deployment automatically runs your build commands and deploys the result whenever you push to your Git repository.

### Add a custom domain
Purchase domains and manage DNS zones and records right inside of Netlify.

### HTTPS is automatic
Your site will automatically be secured with a free TLS certificate from Let’s Encrypt.

### Deploy Previews
Netlify’s Deploy Previews streamlined your workflow by giving you a unique, permanent URL to check what your changes will be like in production whenever you submit a pull request.

### And a lot more!
Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.

Check out the [code infra dashboard](https://code-infra-dashboard.onrender.com/repository/mui/base-ui/prs/5115) for more information about this PR.

# PR review

PR #5115 adds a new `Listbox` component (~8k lines: selection modes, keyboard nav, Pragmatic drag-and-drop, lazy loading, form integration). **There is one merge-blocker:** `itemToStringLabel` is a documented public prop that is wired into the store but has no consumer, so it silently does nothing. Beyond that, the notable items are a confirmed wrong-highlight after non-contiguous multi-select reorder, a first-ArrowDown that skips the first option, a duplicate-key form bug, an RTL gap, a stale group-label id, a double tab-stop, and two large-list perf cliffs. The scariest candidates I chased — composite-index vs. DOM-order desync and a Shift+Arrow double-move — are **non-issues** (composite sorts by `compareDocumentPosition` and bails on Shift). Verification was static (no test run / profiler).

## Bugs (12)

### 1. 🔴 `itemToStringLabel` ships as a no-op public API

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/root/ListboxRoot.tsx:414`

```tsx
itemToStringLabel?: ((itemValue: Value) => string) | undefined;
```

The prop is stored on the Listbox store (`store.ts:14,66`) and passed through Root, but **nothing reads `selectors.itemToStringLabel`**. `labelsRef` (used by typeahead) is populated only from each item's `label` prop or rendered text content (via `useCompositeListItem`). Unlike Combobox — where `itemToStringLabel` is consumed in `ComboboxValue.tsx` — Listbox has no consumer.

**Failure scenario:** A user passes `itemToStringLabel={(item) => item.name}` expecting object-value typeahead to work; matching still fails unless every `Listbox.Item` also has an explicit `label`. The documented prop does nothing.

**Fix:** Wire it into item label registration with `stringifyAsLabel` (so typeahead can match object values), or remove the prop and its docs before release.

### 2. 🟡 Multi-select keyboard reorder highlights/focuses the wrong item for non-contiguous selections

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/item/ListboxItem.tsx:446`

```tsx
const offsetInSelection = selectedIndices.indexOf(resolvedIndex);
const newFirstIdx = moveUp ? firstIdx - 1 : firstIdx + 1;
store.set('activeIndex', newFirstIdx + offsetInSelection);
```

`newFirstIdx = firstIdx ± 1` only equals the moved block's landing index when the selection is **contiguous**. For a non-contiguous selection the highlight (and `restoreFocusAndScroll`, which focuses `[role="option"][tabindex="0"]`) lands on the wrong row. Confirmed by tracing.

**Failure scenario:** `multiple` mode, items `[0,1,2,3,4]`. Toggle-select **1 and 3**, focus item 3, Alt+ArrowDown → items move correctly to `[0,2,4,1,3]` but `activeIndex` is set to 3 (value `1`) while the initiating item is now at index 4. Focus jumps to the wrong item, and a follow-up Alt+Arrow then reorders the wrong item. The contiguous case works.

**Fix:** After the move, recompute the initiating item's index from the registry: `store.set('activeIndex', findItemIndex(valuesRef.current, itemValue, eqFn))`.

### 3. 🟡 First ArrowDown skips the first option

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/list/ListboxList.tsx:50`

```tsx
highlightedIndex: activeIndex ?? 0,
```

When the list container is focused with nothing highlighted, `activeIndex` is `null` so composite is seeded with `highlightedIndex: 0` — but no item is actually highlighted/focused. The first ArrowDown advances *from* the phantom index 0 to index 1 (`useCompositeRoot` treats `nextIndex === highlightedIndex` as "already there" and steps forward).

**Failure scenario:** A keyboard user tabs into a fresh listbox and presses ArrowDown; option 1 is highlighted and option 0 is skipped.

**Fix:** Report the first item as highlighted on list focus, or pass a sentinel (e.g. `null`/`-1` semantics) so the first forward arrow lands on index 0.

### 4. 🟡 Duplicate React keys on hidden inputs drop a form value

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/root/ListboxRoot.tsx:280`

```tsx
return <input key={currentSerializedValue} type="hidden" name={name} value={currentSerializedValue} />;
```

The key is the serialized value, so two selected values that serialize to the same string collide → React drops one input and the form submits fewer values than selected (plus a console warning).

**Failure scenario:** A controlled `value={['a', 'a']}` (controlled mode bypasses the reducer dedup), or two distinct objects with a by-id `isItemEqualToValue` and a non-injective `itemToStringValue` → one `<input>` dropped → `FormData` has one entry instead of two.

**Fix:** Include the index in the key: `` key={`${i}-${currentSerializedValue}`} ``. (The comma-`join` for `serializedValue` is *not* a submission bug — per-value hidden inputs carry submission; the joined string only feeds validity tracking.)

### 5. 🟡 Horizontal Alt+Arrow reorder ignores RTL

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/item/ListboxItem.tsx:317`

```tsx
const moveUp = (isVertical && event.key === 'ArrowUp') || (!isVertical && event.key === 'ArrowLeft');
const moveDown = (isVertical && event.key === 'ArrowDown') || (!isVertical && event.key === 'ArrowRight');
```

`ListboxList.handleSelectionKeyDown` swaps Left/Right for `direction === 'rtl'` (List.tsx:155-161), but this keyboard-reorder handler does not.

**Failure scenario:** Horizontal listbox with `dir="rtl"` and DnD enabled — ArrowLeft reorders the opposite direction from how Shift+Arrow navigates the same widget.

**Fix:** Mirror the RTL swap: in horizontal RTL, ArrowRight → `before`/moveUp, ArrowLeft → `after`/moveDown.

### 6. 🟡 Group labels leave a stale `aria-labelledby`

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/group-label/ListboxGroupLabel.tsx:25`

```tsx
useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
  setLabelId(id);
}, [id, setLabelId]);
```

Unlike `MenuGroupLabel` and `ComboboxGroupLabel` (both `return () => setLabelId(undefined)`), this effect never unregisters the id.

**Failure scenario:** A conditional `Listbox.GroupLabel` unmounts and the parent group keeps `aria-labelledby` pointing at a removed element.

**Fix:** `return () => setLabelId(undefined);`

### 7. 🟡 Double tab stop: list container and roving item both `tabIndex={0}`

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/list/ListboxList.tsx:233` + `packages/react/src/listbox/item/ListboxItem.tsx:478`

The list is permanently `tabIndex: disabled ? undefined : 0` and items use roving tabindex (`highlighted ? 0 : -1`) with real DOM focus (no `aria-activedescendant`). When an item is highlighted, both the container and that item are in the tab order. Sibling `Combobox.List` uses `tabIndex: -1` (ComboboxList.tsx:76).

**Failure scenario:** With a highlighted item, Tab into the listbox stops on the container, then on the option — an extra, semantically empty stop.

**Fix:** Set the container `tabIndex={-1}` once items can take the roving stop (keep `0` only for the empty-list case); confirm the intended focus model first.

### 8. 🟡 Typeahead can't cycle on a repeated character and skips the current item

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/list/ListboxList.tsx:85,95`

```tsx
typeaheadStringRef.current += event.key.toLowerCase();
// ...
const startIndex = activeIndex != null ? activeIndex + 1 : 0;
```

The comment claims "typing the same character repeatedly cycles through matches," but the buffer always appends, so pressing `a` then `a` searches for `aa` and cannot cycle through `Apple`, `Apricot`, … Separately, starting at `activeIndex + 1` means a growing multi-char buffer can jump away from a still-matching current item.

**Failure scenario:** Repeatedly pressing the same starting letter stops matching instead of cycling through same-initial options.

**Fix:** Special-case a single repeated-character buffer to cycle from `activeIndex + 1`, and start at `activeIndex` (inclusive) for genuine multi-char searches — or reuse the existing `useTypeahead` behavior.

### 9. 🟡 `onHighlightChange` runs a full `querySelectorAll` on every store mutation

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/utils/useHighlightChangeNotifier.ts:61` (called from `store.subscribe` at :116)

```tsx
const element = listEl?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[role="option"]')[activeIndex] ?? null;
```

The subscription fires on every `store.set` (selection, hover, drag, loading), and `resolveHighlightedItem` walks all N option nodes *before* the `areHighlightsEqual` early-out — even when `activeIndex` didn't change. O(N) DOM query per mutation, only when `onHighlightChange` is set.

**Failure scenario:** A 5k-item listbox with an `onHighlightChange` handler; holding ArrowDown or rapid hover does a full DOM walk per event.

**Fix:** Gate on an actual `activeIndex` change (`store.observe('activeIndex', …)`) and resolve the element from `composite.elementsRef` rather than re-querying.

### 10. 🟡 Every item re-registers with Pragmatic DnD on any reorder

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/utils/useDragAndDrop.ts:60-87` (effect deps include `index`, `itemValue`)

The setup `useIsoLayoutEffect` tears down and re-creates `draggable()` + `dropTargetForElements()` whenever `index` changes; a reorder shifts the index of every item between source and target. The handlers already read live data from refs/store.

**Failure scenario:** Dragging the first item of a 2k-item list to the bottom re-registers ~2k items synchronously post-drop → visible hitch.

**Fix:** Read `index`/`itemValue` from refs (the component has `indexRef`) inside the Pragmatic callbacks and drop them from the effect deps.

### 11. ℹ️ Smaller correctness/realm notes

- **Stale closure `index`** in `onClick`/`onFocus`/`onMouseMove` (`ListboxItem.tsx:480,484,525`) — only keydown re-resolves via `findItemIndex`; a click/hover in the window between an optimistic registry reorder and React re-render can act on a stale index.
- **`IntersectionObserver` uses the global constructor** (`ListboxLoadingTrigger.tsx:76`) instead of `ownerWindow(root).IntersectionObserver` — wrong realm inside a cross-document iframe/portal (AGENTS.md owner-utilities rule); SSR-safe otherwise.
- **Non-memoized selectors** (`store.ts`) — `isSelected` does `value.some(...)` per item, so a toggle in `multiple` mode is O(N·M) in `getSnapshot`; `createSelectorMemoized` would short-circuit on unchanged `value`.

### 12. ℹ️ API-design footguns on the new public surface (hard to reverse post-release)

- **`value` is always `Value[]`, even in `'single'` mode** (`ListboxRoot.tsx:424`) — `Select`/`Combobox` give a scalar in single mode; the single-select hero demo is forced into `defaultValue={['billie-jean']}` and consumers read `value[0]` everywhere.
- **`selectionMode: 'single' | 'multiple' | 'explicit-multiple'`** vs. the library-wide public `multiple` boolean (Combobox maps it internally); `'explicit-multiple'` is undiscoverable by name.
- **`onHighlightChange(value, element)`** exposes a raw `HTMLElement` positionally, whereas the sibling ships `onItemHighlighted(value, eventDetails)` with a `reason` (`ComboboxRoot.tsx:127`); `actionsRef.highlightValue(value, element?)` similarly leaks keyed-reconciliation internals.

## Tests (2)

### 1. 🟡 Core public behaviors ship with no test

Several headline behaviors are uncovered, so a regression in any would stay green: **multi-select Alt+Arrow reorder** (including the non-contiguous case from bug #2), **single-item pointer-drag reorder** (only multi-drag/`canDrop=false`/drop-on-self are tested), **`actionsRef.highlightValue`**, **Escape-to-clear** and **Ctrl+A toggle-all**, **autofill `onChange`** resolution, **`required`/form-submission round-trip** (incl. a duplicate value, which exercises bug #4), and **typeahead reset/wrap/cycle**. Gate layout-dependent cases in Chromium via `it.skipIf(isJSDOM)`.

### 2. 🟡 Split the multi-assertion `waitFor`

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/drag-and-drop-provider/ListboxDragAndDropProvider.test.tsx:131`

```tsx
await waitFor(() => {
  expect(screen.getAllByRole('option').map((el) => el.textContent)).toEqual([...]);
  expect(screen.getByRole('option', { name: 'b' })).toBe(document.activeElement);
});
```

AGENTS.md asks for one assertion per `waitFor` so retries stay scoped. **Fix:** Use separate `waitFor` calls for the order and the focus assertions.

## Simplifications (4)

### 1. 🟡 Re-use `selectedValueIncludes` instead of hand-rolling `.some(eqFn)`

`packages/react/src/internals/itemEquality.ts` exports `selectedValueIncludes(values, item, comparer)` (with null guards), re-implemented at ~5 sites: `store.ts:82`, `ListboxList.tsx:211`, `ListboxItem.tsx:423`, `ListboxDragAndDropProvider.tsx:158,168`. **Fix:** Call the helper; several sites can drop their `compareItemEquality` import.

### 2. 🟡 Dead `policySignature` field on the DnD context

**Location:** `ListboxDragAndDropProviderContext.ts:41` + `ListboxDragAndDropProvider.tsx:326`. Declared and constructed but never read (and it pins `canDrag, canDrop` in the memo deps). **Fix:** Delete it.

### 3. 🟡 Raw `setTimeout` in `restoreFocusAndScroll` bypasses the `useTimeout` lifecycle

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/item/ListboxItem.tsx:347`. The code documents *why* it avoids `useTimeout` (the item can unmount during a cross-group reorder and a hook timer would be canceled). The trade-off is a real, uncancelable timer that can run post-unmount against stale state (it mostly no-ops against the external store). **Fix:** Move the scheduler to a root/provider-scoped callback (which doesn't unmount mid-reorder) using `useTimeout`/`afterDomSettle`, keeping the cross-group robustness without a raw timer.

### 4. ℹ️ Dead/duplicated state

- **`typingRef`** (`store.ts:49`, written in `ListboxList` typeahead) is never read — remove it, or use it to suppress hover-steal during typeahead (the likely intent).
- The "iterate values, skip undefined/disabled" predicate (`selectAll`, Ctrl+A pre-check, DnD multi-drag), the "collect selected indices" loop (Item reorder vs. DnD provider), and the 4× `reorderRegistry` pass over 4 parallel arrays can each collapse to one shared helper.

## Docs (2)

### 1. 🟡 DnD-context error message is terser than its siblings

**Location:** `packages/react/src/listbox/drag-and-drop-provider/ListboxDragAndDropProviderContext.ts:59` — `'… is missing. Use <Listbox.DragAndDropProvider>.'` drops the convention the other three Listbox context errors use. **Fix:** `'Base UI: ListboxDragAndDropProviderContext is missing. Listbox drag-and-drop parts must be placed within <Listbox.DragAndDropProvider>.'`, then re-run `pnpm extract-error-codes` (same arg count → update code 99 in place).

### 2. ℹ️ Smaller doc gaps

- **DnD payload type shapes are not rendered.** `types.md:321-323` references `ListboxDragAndDropItem<Value>` and `ListboxDragAndDropProviderOnItemsReorderEvent<Value>` in the prop table, but only `ListboxDragAndDropTargetEdge` is rendered (`:411`). Users can't see that items expose `{ value, index, groupId, disabled }` or that reorder events carry `reason`. Add those shapes.
- The substantial multi-select keyboard contract (Shift+Arrow, Ctrl/Cmd+A, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Home/End, Escape) is implemented but **undocumented** on `listbox/page.mdx` (only Alt+Arrow is mentioned).
- The "two render cycles" comments (`ListboxRoot.tsx:191`, `useHighlightChangeNotifier.ts:20`) understate the actual `afterDomSettle` mechanism (a macrotask + two animation frames).

## Verdict

**Request changes** — the no-op `itemToStringLabel` public prop (#1) should be wired up or removed before this new API ships; the multi-select-reorder highlight (#2), first-ArrowDown skip (#3), and duplicate-key form bug (#4) are the next most worth fixing.
